input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, the conclusion remains SUPPORTED. 

H1 (one-time items affecting the margin): CHALLENGE_REFUTED. Evidence E2 explicitly states that the 28.7% operating margin for FY2025 already reflects "other operating charges" in its calculation, as operating margin is defined as operating income divided by net operating revenues after considering all operating charges. The evidence indicates that 2025 actually benefited from LOWER other operating charges compared to 2024 (which had a large fairlife contingent consideration remeasurement). This means the 28.7% figure is the GAAP operating margin that properly includes all charges, and if anything, 2024's margin was more affected by one-time items than 2025's.

H2 (adjusted/non-GAAP margin): NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE. The retrieved evidence (E15, E16, E17) does not provide any adjusted or non-GAAP operating margin figures that differ from the reported 28.7%. The passages discuss performance criteria for compensation and gross profit margins, but no alternative operating margin calculation is presented.

H3 (restatement): NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE. The retrieved evidence (E18, E19, E20) discusses stock-based compensation, gross profit margins, and other operating charges, but contains no indication of any restatement or correction to the fiscal year 2025 operating margin figures.

The claim that Coca-Cola's operating margin for fiscal year 2025 exceeded 25% is directly supported by E2 showing a consolidated operating margin of 28.7% for the year ended December 31, 2025. This is corroborated by the computed figures (E7: operating income of $13,762 million; E8: revenue of $47,941 million; yielding 28.7%). Since 28.7% > 25%, the claim is supported.
